name: Constant Curvature Black Holes
description: Anti-de Sitter space of four or more dimensions with its points identified along a boost, a black hole of constant negative curvature whose event horizon in four dimensions is a torus that grows in time.
convention: No coordinate has dimensions of time, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: The orbits of a boost in anti-de Sitter space are spacelike in one region, null on a hyperboloid, and timelike beyond it, and with points identified along them the region of spacelike orbits is a black hole of constant negative curvature [banados1998]. In three dimensions the space identified in the same way is the spinless black hole of Máximo Bañados, Claudio Teitelboim, and Jorge Zanelli [banados1998, aminneborg1996]. Stefan Åminneborg, Ingemar Bengtsson, Sören Holst, and Peter Peldán built the hole of four dimensions in 1996 by rotating that spinless hole about an axis [aminneborg1996]. Its space has one asymptotic region, and its event horizon grows from a circle at the moment of time symmetry into a torus [aminneborg1996].¶Holst and Peldán classified the quotients of anti-de Sitter space by a single generator in three and four dimensions in 1997, sorting the Killing fields of $SO(2,3)$ into types [holst1997]. In four dimensions only the quotient by one type, a single boost, has an event horizon, and the analogue of the rotating hole of three dimensions has none, since the extra dimension of space leaves infinity connected [holst1997]. No Killing field is timelike throughout the exterior, so the hole is not static [holst1997]. Its toroidal horizon grows along one cycle at constant length along the other, so the horizon shears and its area increases [holst1997]. Inside, Holst and Peldán found closed trapped tori on the slices of their interior chart, from the singularity up to an apparent horizon halfway to the event horizon in the chart's timelike coordinate [holst1997]. They gave its symmetry group as $SO(1,2)\times U(1)$ and suggested that the growing hole "may turn out to be valuable as a toy model in different areas" [holst1997].¶Bañados wrote the quotient in $n$ dimensions in Kruskal coordinates in 1998, and at $n = 3$ the metric is the spinless hole of three dimensions [banados1998]. Its horizon is the hypercone on which the squared norm of the boost equals $r_+^2$, $r_+$ being the radius of each circle on the horizon [banados1998]. The hyperboloid on which the norm vanishes is a singularity, because the region beyond it holds closed timelike curves and is removed [banados1998]. The topology is $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times S^1$, and a picture of the causal structure takes $n - 1$ dimensions, each of its points a circle [banados1998]. Bañados found every conserved charge of the hole infinite in Einstein's theory and embedded the hole of five dimensions in a Chern-Simons supergravity for $SU(2,2|N)$, where its mass $M$ and angular momentum $J$ are finite [banados1998]. There the two charges are reversed relative to the hole of three dimensions, the horizon exists for $J \ge M$, and the entropy is $4\pi k r_-$, with $k$ the fixed value of a $U(1)$ field strength and $r_-$ a second length of the rotating hole [banados1998].¶Bañados, Andrés Gomberoff, and Cristián Martínez wrote the hole of four dimensions in Kruskal coordinates in 1998, one patch of which covers the whole black hole since its infinity is connected [banados1998gomberoff]. Their static coordinates cover only part of the exterior, and a chart that depends on time covers all of it, every slice of constant angle a spinless hole of three dimensions [banados1998gomberoff]. Taking circles as the closed surfaces, Bañados, Gomberoff, and Martínez found every circle beyond the future horizon trapped, with no apparent horizon of the kind Holst and Peldán had found [banados1998gomberoff]. The Euclidean section is thermal anti-de Sitter space with the identified angle as its time [banados1998gomberoff]. In five dimensions they built a rotating hole, together with its extreme limit, its holonomies, and the Killing spinors that survive the identification [banados1998gomberoff]. José Figueroa-O'Farrill, Owen Madden, Simon F. Ross, and Joan Simón showed in 2004 that in four or more dimensions a quotient by one generator is a black hole only for a boost, alone or with rotations, and that this rotating hole has no event horizon [figueroa2004].¶Jolien Creighton and Robert Mann computed the entropy of the hole of four dimensions from the Einstein-Hilbert action in 1998, inside a quasilocal surface around it [creighton1998]. It depends on the size of that surface and vanishes as the surface approaches the horizon, and since the temperature varies over the surface and diverges on its axis, the first law holds only in integral form [creighton1998]. Rong-Gen Cai studied the hole of five dimensions through the correspondence between gravity in anti-de Sitter space and conformal field theory in 2002 [cai2002constant]. Its boundary is a de Sitter space of three dimensions times a circle, and the stress tensor of the dual field theory there has zero trace and a negative energy density [cai2002constant]. Cai also identified the hole with the bubble of nothing continued from the Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter hole at zero mass [cai2002constant]. Ross and Georgina Titchener argued in 2005 that the event horizon of the hole of five dimensions, which is not a Killing horizon, has no entropy, and that the Euclidean vacuum is the only regular invariant vacuum of a free scalar field there [ross2005].¶Jan Åman, Åminneborg, Bengtsson, and Narit Pidokrajt placed the hole of four dimensions in 2008 in two families of one parameter each from the Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter solution, one of bubbles of nothing and one of black holes free of curvature singularities, all with zero conserved charges [aman2008]. Åminneborg and Bengtsson gave a definition of such quotient black holes the same year and upheld, with an argument of their own, the conclusion of Holst and Peldán that the quotient by a boost combined with a rotation has closed timelike curves and is no black hole [aminneborg2008]. Cai and Yun Soo Myung found in 2011, from an embedding of the hole of five dimensions in a flat space of six, the same Hawking temperature in its static chart and in the chart of its whole exterior, equal to that of the de Sitter space on its boundary [cai2011]. Pablo Guilleminot, Rodrigo Olea, and Alexander Petrov found in 2017 that the hole has zero mass and angular momentum in Einstein gravity in every dimension from four up, with a vacuum energy alone in odd dimensions, and that the boost with which Bañados added rotation changes none of its charges [guilleminot2017]. The same three found its Euclidean action zero in even dimensions and, reading the hole as an extended object that contains a de Sitter space of $n - 2$ dimensions, concluded in 2018 that it has no mass, angular momentum, or entropy [guilleminot2018]. Ankit Anand, Ruben Campos Delgado, and Daris Samart took a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ quotient of the hole in 2025 and found that a massive vector field with suitable boundary conditions round a noncontractible cycle makes the averaged null energy negative, so that the wormhole of the quotient becomes traversable [anand2025].

related.text: The space these black holes are quotients of, by the group that one boost generates, so the two are the same at every point [banados1998].
The black hole of three dimensions, made by identifying points of anti-de Sitter space in the same way. Without rotation it is the Kruskal metric of these holes in three dimensions [banados1998].

Black holes that Åminneborg, Bengtsson, Holst, and Peldán made by identifying points of anti-de Sitter space in the same 1996 paper as the toroidal hole of four dimensions, with horizons of genus two or more [aminneborg1996].

The black hole of anti-de Sitter space with a curvature singularity at its centre. Continued analytically into a bubble of nothing with its mass set to zero, and with points identified, it becomes the hole of four dimensions [aman2008, cai2002constant].
Flat space with its points identified by a boost. Anti-de Sitter space identified in the same way is a black hole [banados1998].
Anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions cut along timelike surfaces and glued back together, into many black holes or one with a wormhole inside, each of constant curvature as these holes are.

coordinates.name: Kruskal

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/l^2$ in four dimensions and $\Lambda = -6/l^2$ in five
Horizon radius, a length, the radius of each circle on the horizon
Radius of the circle of $\varphi$, a length

coordinates.convention: We use Bañados, Gomberoff, and Martínez's Kruskal coordinates $(y_0, y_1, y_2, \varphi)$, all dimensionless, with $\varphi$ the identified angle.
geodesics: \ddot{\varphi} + \dfrac{8y_0}{\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 + 1\right)\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - 1\right)}\dot{y_0}\dot{\varphi} - \dfrac{8y_1}{\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 + 1\right)\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - 1\right)}\dot{y_1}\dot{\varphi} - \dfrac{8y_2}{\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 + 1\right)\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - 1\right)}\dot{y_2}\dot{\varphi} = 0

coordinates.name: Static

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/l^2$ in four dimensions and $\Lambda = -6/l^2$ in five
Horizon radius, a length, the radius of each circle on the horizon

coordinates.convention: We use Bañados, Gomberoff, and Martínez's static coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \varphi)$, with $r$ a length and $t$, $\theta$, and $\varphi$ dimensionless.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\sin^2\theta}{l^2}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{r}{\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}{r_+^2}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}{l^2}\dot{\varphi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Exterior

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/l^2$ in four dimensions and $\Lambda = -6/l^2$ in five
Horizon radius, a length, the radius of each circle on the horizon

coordinates.convention: We use Bañados, Gomberoff, and Martínez's coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \varphi)$ of the whole exterior, with $r$ a length and $t$, $\theta$, and $\varphi$ dimensionless.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}{l^2}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{r}{\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\cosh^2\left(\dfrac{r_+\,t}{l}\right)}{r_+^2}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}{l^2}\dot{\varphi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Holst-Peldán Interior

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/l^2$ in four dimensions and $\Lambda = -6/l^2$ in five
Horizon radius, a length, the radius of each circle on the horizon

coordinates.convention: We use Holst and Peldán's coordinates $(r, t, \psi, \varphi)$ of the interior, all dimensionless, with their unit radius restored as $l$. Their $r$ is the radius of the Kruskal chart divided by $r_+$, their $\psi$ is $r_+/l$ times the identified angle $\varphi$ of the other charts, and their $\varphi$ is the angle $\theta$ of the exterior chart.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = l^2\left(-\dfrac{dr^2}{1 - r^2} + \left(1 - r^2\right)dt^2 + r^2d\psi^2 + \left(1 - r^2\right)\sinh^2t\,d\varphi^2\right)
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{r}{\left(1 + r\right)\left(1 - r\right)}\dot{r}^2 - r\left(1 + r\right)\left(1 - r\right)\dot{t}^2 + r\left(1 + r\right)\left(1 - r\right)\dot{\psi}^2 - r\left(1 + r\right)\left(1 - r\right)\sinh^2 t\,\dot{\varphi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Holst-Peldán Null

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/l^2$ in four dimensions and $\Lambda = -6/l^2$ in five
Horizon radius, a length, the radius of each circle on the horizon
Sum of the null coordinates
Difference of the null coordinates

coordinates.convention: We use Holst and Peldán's null coordinates $(u, v, \psi, \varphi)$, all dimensionless, with $\tan u = e^{-t}\sqrt{(1 - r)/(1 + r)}$ and $\tan v = e^t\sqrt{(1 - r)/(1 + r)}$ in the interior chart and their unit radius restored as $l$.

coordinates.name: Kruskal, Five Dimensions
domains: y_0^2 = y_1^2 + y_2^2 + y_3^2 \;\text{(the event horizon)}

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/l^2$ in four dimensions and $\Lambda = -6/l^2$ in five
Horizon radius, a length, the radius of each circle on the horizon
Radius of the circle of $\varphi$, a length

coordinates.convention: We use Bañados's Kruskal coordinates $(y_0, y_1, y_2, y_3, \varphi)$ of five dimensions, all dimensionless, with $\varphi$ the identified angle.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = \dfrac{l^2\left(r + r_+\right)^2}{r_+^2}\left(-dy_0^2 + dy_1^2 + dy_2^2 + dy_3^2\right) + r^2d\varphi^2
geodesics: \ddot{\varphi} + \dfrac{8y_0}{\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - y_3^2 + 1\right)\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - y_3^2 - 1\right)}\dot{y_0}\dot{\varphi} - \dfrac{8y_1}{\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - y_3^2 + 1\right)\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - y_3^2 - 1\right)}\dot{y_1}\dot{\varphi} - \dfrac{8y_2}{\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - y_3^2 + 1\right)\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - y_3^2 - 1\right)}\dot{y_2}\dot{\varphi} - \dfrac{8y_3}{\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - y_3^2 + 1\right)\left(y_0^2 - y_1^2 - y_2^2 - y_3^2 - 1\right)}\dot{y_3}\dot{\varphi} = 0

coordinates.name: Static, Five Dimensions

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/l^2$ in four dimensions and $\Lambda = -6/l^2$ in five
Horizon radius, a length, the radius of each circle on the horizon

coordinates.convention: We use Bañados's static coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \chi, \varphi)$ of five dimensions, with $r$ a length and $t$, $\theta$, $\chi$, and $\varphi$ dimensionless.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\cos^2\theta}{l^2}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{r}{\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}{r_+^2}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\sin^2\theta}{r_+^2}\dot{\chi}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}{l^2}\dot{\varphi}^2 = 0

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/l^2$ in four dimensions and $\Lambda = -6/l^2$ in five
Horizon radius, a length, the radius of each circle on the horizon

coordinates.convention: We use Cai's coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \chi, \varphi)$ of the whole exterior in five dimensions, with $r$ a length and $t$, $\theta$, $\chi$, and $\varphi$ dimensionless.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}{l^2}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{r}{\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\cosh^2\left(\dfrac{r_+\,t}{l}\right)}{r_+^2}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)\cosh^2\left(\dfrac{r_+\,t}{l}\right)\sin^2\theta}{r_+^2}\dot{\chi}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r + r_+\right)\left(r - r_+\right)}{l^2}\dot{\varphi}^2 = 0
